answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards; a kernel contract records the lock and slashes it when fraud is proven through an appealable evidence process. One person can still create many identities, so this is not identity proof: each duplicate must tie up capital and risks losing it. That makes a sybil attack costly, especially when fake agents must sustain a sonnet of plausible histories or coordinate an onyx-scale swarm.
